title: The Watermelon Woman (1996)-- masterful indie cinema

commenti.body: Masterful is definitely not a word I would apply to this movie.  It's on the level of *Clerks* in terms of technique and acting - that is, not great, often not even very good.  But the script is fun, the jokes are great, and much of the craft is quite technically solid for what was basically an amateur film.  Worth watching for its significance to the indie film and queer cinema, and an enjoyable watch at that.

Yes, it is definitely a low budget movie and it shows. I thought that the idea to make the main characters amateur filmmakers themselves is a great way of getting the audience to suspend disbelief.

We see them bumble their way through filmmaking within the movie. Somehow this makes the rough edges of the film far more acceptable in a meta way.

Fun and funny. I think it's a very heartwarming film, especially, of course, for queer women of color, because it's self-narrativizing in a way that's holistic, sincere and affectionate. Actual lesbian sex! Inter-community frustrations! That lesbian book archive brought me to tears laughing. People who get so bent out of shape about perceiving history through the lens of modernity might benefit from seeing this, from seeing that the whole point of looking back at history is to understand ourselves more now.

I think this is a film that really shows how integral video rental stores were to community and shared culture in the nineties. And that's always a great way to frame and set a film about films.

Well said! Thanks for your comment. The film as a whole is a nice bit of myth-making.

The video store element is a good point too. Looking back from the 2020s, the contemporary parts of the movie have become historical too. The shared space of the video store is gone now, replaced in some ways by the internet when it comes to sharing and discussing movies.
